Refreshed against current main. Both P1 findings from the 75e7b59f1b80 review are fixed in the diff, each with its own regression case and its own before/after trace in the body.

**[P1] Serialize the hash check with the agent-file write.** Fixed at the boundary you named. `enqueueWorkspaceFileUpdate` in `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-fs.ts` is now exported and owns the agent-file compare-and-write, so `agents.files.set` shares the one queue that already serializes `sessions.files.set` instead of duplicating an unserialized copy. One agent workspace file is reachable from both routes, so a per-route queue would not have closed it. Concurrent-save coverage added in `agents-files.test.ts`; it fails on the reviewed head with `expected [ { ok: true, ...(2) }, ...(1) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2`. The body carries a real two-writer trace against the reviewed head and against this head.

**[P1] Prevent conflict reload from authorizing the stale draft.** Fixed. The forced reload that refreshed the base hash while keeping the draft is removed. A refused write keeps the hash it was refused against, so a repeated Save is refused again rather than winning. Resolution is now explicit: the conflict callout offers Reload (take the workspace version, drop the draft) and Overwrite (re-read the current hash, then deliberately replace the workspace version), the same two-button contract `chat-detail-panel.ts` already uses for `session_file_conflict`. Second-Save coverage added in `ui/src/pages/agents/files.test.ts`, plus reload and overwrite cases.

**Real Control UI proof.** Added. The body carries a trace from real headless Chromium driving the real Control UI bundle against a real Gateway on a loopback port and a real agent workspace on disk, run on pristine main 82a74b113c4f and on this head with identical inputs. On main the Save lands silently and the agent's appended line is erased; here the Save is refused, the callout names the file and offers Reload and Overwrite, and a second click leaves the workspace bytes untouched. `ui/src/e2e/agent-file-lifecycle.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` now also carries the conflict, Overwrite and Reload flow so this stays covered.

The three merge-risk items map onto the two findings and the proof above.

One gap left open deliberately, stated in the body: a file that does not exist yet has no base token to send, so an operator Save that creates a bootstrap file can still race an agent creating the same file first. Closing that needs an `expectedAbsent` precondition on the protocol, which is a wider surface change than this fix and a maintainer call.

New head: 82fdee3d9d857ef7b7ca38d7de633a3c4646b0bc.

The round-2 finding was correct and is fixed. New head: 3c4f9367b2fc4be81e15c26668940451dad4e7bb, rebased onto 4e330557ae33.

**[P1] Preserve the dirty draft's base hash across Refresh.** The stored hash is now the draft's write precondition rather than the base's. It advances only when the draft advances with it: on a write, on an explicit Reload or Overwrite, or on a read that rebases a clean draft. `loadAgentFiles(agentId, true)` from the Core Files Refresh button still refreshes the displayed base and still spares a dirty draft, but that draft keeps the precondition it was actually typed against, so the following Save is refused. Refresh also no longer dismisses a standing conflict, and the callout carries its own copy so it survives the cleared error.

Coverage added in `ui/src/pages/agents/files.test.ts`: dirty Refresh then Save, clean Refresh adopting the new hash, and conflict survival through Refresh. The first and third fail on 82fdee3d9d85 for their own reasons (draft carrying `bbbb...` instead of `aaaa...`, and `expected null to be 'AGENTS.md'`); the clean-Refresh case passes on both heads, so the existing rebase-a-clean-draft contract is unchanged. `ui/src/e2e/agent-file-lifecycle.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` now also drives Refresh-then-Save.

**Live reproduction of the finding, and of the fix.** The same browser driver ran unchanged against three trees. On 82fdee3d9d85 the two Saves were refused as intended, then Refresh-then-Save wrote `"# Persona\n- operator note\n"`, discarding both the agent's memory and the line appended after it. On this head the same clicks leave `"# Persona\n- agent learned the operator's birthday\n- a later memory\n"` on disk with the draft still in the editor. On pristine main the very first Save clobbers with no callout. All three traces are in the body.

One note on gates: the whole-graph `oxlint:core` shard exhausts this machine's memory, so I ran the same type-aware lane scoped to every changed file with `--tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` instead, clean. `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:core:test`, `ui:i18n:verify` and both protocol guards are clean, and CI will run the full shard.

Still open and deliberate, unchanged from the last round: a file that does not exist yet has no base token, so an operator Save that creates a bootstrap file can still race an agent creating the same file first. Closing that needs an `expectedAbsent` protocol precondition, which is a maintainer call rather than something to fold in here.
